stem: Why can offspring from the same two heterozygous parents differ genetically from one another?
choices: Segregation and recombination create different allele combinations
Each offspring receives the same parental alleles but expresses them differently because environmental conditions alter inheritance during fertilization
Heterozygous parents tend to transmit complete chromosome sets without recombination, so differences among offspring mainly reflect later growth conditions
Genetic variation among siblings arises when the maternal parent changes which traits are inherited after fertilization has occurred
rationale: During sexual reproduction, alleles segregate and chromosomes recombine, generating different genetic combinations among offspring.
